body.statement:
Open-ended Question 6.  Put \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\), and let \(\mathscr G_J\) be the profiled residual functional in the second-order pair-orbit selection handle.  Establish, or refute by exact finite-orbit certificates, an equicoercive second-order epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit and use its minimizer contact set to characterize \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\).  When \(\rho=1/2\) and \(\kappa_J\to\kappa\in\mathbb R\), determine whether the limit on \(\mathcal F_{1/2}\) is the unrestricted Airy/local-experiment functional \(\mathscr A(\mu)\) plus
\[
 \kappa\!\left(2\int m\,d\mu-1\right).
\]
This expression is presently only upper-bound evidence; a matching lower expansion is required.  Treat \(\kappa_J\to+\infty\), \(\kappa_J\to-\infty\), and \(\rho>1/2\) as separate regimes.  Prove recovery by exact finite minimizers only after the corresponding liminf, recovery-sequence, and compactness statements are established; finite-grid contact patterns alone do not determine the limit set.

obligation.what_is_open: For each path with \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\), prove a matching second-order liminf and recovery theorem for the profiled residual risks and then show that the minimizer contact set is necessary and sufficient for weak limits of exact finite minimizers.
obligation.obstruction: The established first-order game is flat on \(\mathcal F_\rho\). The exact finite conic certificates compute each fixed-\(J\) face but do not yield uniform second-order expansions. At \(\rho=1/2\), the hard-budget correction and unrestricted Airy correction compete only when \(\kappa_J=(s_J-J/2)/J^{2/3}\) is finite; the current core has neither the local pair-orbit kernel nor a matching lower expansion needed to promote the candidate upper-bound term into an epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit.
obligation.attempted: The scalar and two-parameter shrinking-prior experiments, including singular boundary information, give the sharp first-order value and envelope. Expanding those information bounds does not distinguish measures sharing the balance and mean-mixed constraints. Exact enumeration at \(J=2,3,4\) shows changing critical contact patterns and therefore cannot certify a stable exact-minimizer selection rule.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact finite contact system in Theorem 1 makes every set \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s_J)\) computable, and Theorem 5 proves
\[
 \mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\subseteq\mathcal F_\rho.
\]
Theorem 5 also recovers every \(\mu\in\mathcal F_\rho\) by invariant procedures whose excess worst risk is \(o(J^{-1})\).  At the critical boundary, writing \(\bar m_J=\int m\,d\mu_{q_J}\), the proposed hard-budget correction obeys the exact rescaling identity
\[
 J^{4/3}\frac{(2\bar m_J-1)(s_J-J/2)}{J^2}
 =\kappa_J(2\bar m_J-1).
\]
Thus finite \(\kappa_J\) is the only scale on which that correction and a \(J^{-4/3}\) unrestricted Airy correction can compete.  This calculation isolates the candidate penalty but does not prove its matching lower expansion, epi- or \(\Gamma\)-convergence, or replacement of first-order-optimal procedures by exact finite minimizers.

body.justification: Exact finite optimizers may select a strict subset of the flat first-order face. The only scale at which the critical hard-budget correction and unrestricted Airy correction can compete is \(\kappa_J=(s_J-J/2)/J^{2/3}\), which makes the residual epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit the precise unresolved object.
body.gap: No established result supplies a uniform second-order lower expansion, equicoercivity, or exact-minimizer recovery for this measure-valued pair-orbit face. Finite-grid contact patterns and first-order \(o(J^{-1})\)-recovery do not fill that gap.
body.consumer: A valid solution would give a principled tie-breaker among first-order-equivalent assignment laws and would state separately what exact minimizers can approach for finite \(\kappa\), the two infinite-\(\kappa\) directions, and \(\rho>1/2\).
